summary: Two independent fresh projects proved that live DeepSeek can ask targeted questions, avoid psychological overreach, persist exact user quotes, and produce real-scene material previews. Earlier failures remain in the denominator: an older runtime misclassified an explicit do-not-move constraint, and the first semantic-guard repair rejected a valid correction after six provider attempts. A final authorized rerun against the next current runtime repaired that exact path and produced a legal linen-sofa preview with one object material diff, zero surface or rule diffs, and all requested locks retained.

failureLedger.description: One assistant reply combined two questions instead of resolving one important ambiguity.
Explicit transform/material locks were recorded as no_new_objects.

Valid same-quote lock_material plus lock_transform repair was rejected after six provider attempts; the next current runtime accepted the same natural-language semantics and produced the requested isolated sofa-material preview.

The failed correction triggered six provider calls and 72,516 total tokens. The next runtime used two attempts with a concrete new validation observation and succeeded in 5.505 seconds; the original amplification remains in the denominator.
The hidden GUI wait predicate remained busy for 115 seconds although the server trace later showed a 22.649-second completed response; browser console contained no matching error.
